headline: Bangladesh dominates world No. 1 Australia in rare Test match
summary: After bowling Australia out for 198 and posting a massive 426, Bangladesh is on the verge of a historic victory on Australian soil.
details: Bangladesh is on the verge of a historic Test victory against the world's No. 1 ranked side, Australia, in a match being played at Darwin's Marrara Stadium.
The Tigers' pace attack, led by Hasan Mahmud's six-wicket haul, first bowled the hosts out for 198 in the first innings.

Bangladesh responded with a dominant batting performance, scoring 426. Tanzid Hasan scored a maiden century in only his second Test, while captain Najmul Hossain Shanto added 84 and Mehidy Hasan Miraz contributed 65.

Australia, in their second innings, struggled early on, losing four wickets for 74 runs. Although Cameron Green and Alex Carey have steadied the ship, they remain trailing by 67 runs at the stumps on day three.
A victory here would be a rare feat for an Asian side visiting Australia. India waited 71 years for their first series win, while Sri Lanka has never won a Test match in Australia.
This match serves as a reminder of Bangladesh's recurring role as the team that forces cricket's superpowers to create a seismic shift in their rebuilding processes after major upsets.
The result will provide significant context to the World Test Championship, as the No. 9 ranked team challenges the world's top-ranked side.

headline_marked: 20-year-old [[salesman stabbed to death]] in Old Dhaka
headline: 20-year-old salesman stabbed to death in Old Dhaka
summary: The victim, Mitul, was allegedly killed by shop employees over a previous quarrel at the East Bengal Supermarket near Sadarghat.
details: A 20-year-old salesman named Mitul was stabbed to death on Saturday evening at the East Bengal Supermarket near Dhaka’s Sadarghat.
According to Sutrapur Police Station Inspector Mehmenul Islam, a group of employees from different shops allegedly stabbed Mitul in the chest with a pair of scissors around 8:30 pm.
The attack was reportedly motivated by a previous enmity; Mitul had allegedly slapped someone from the market during a quarrel two days prior.
Police recovered the body and sent it to the Sir Salimullah Medical College Mitford Hospital morgue for an autopsy.
Following the incident, several hundred agitated people, including the victim's relatives, held a procession from Sadarghat to Mitford Hospital.
Mitul was identified as a Jatiotabadi Swechchhasebak Dal activist of Dhaka Metropolitan South’s Ward 37.
caption:
A 20-year-old salesman was stabbed to death in Old Dhaka over a quarrel that happened two days prior.

A 20-year-old salesman named Mitul was stabbed to death on Saturday evening at the East Bengal Supermarket near Dhaka’s Sadarghat.

According to Sutrapur Police Station Inspector Mehmenul Islam, a group of employees from different shops allegedly stabbed Mitul in the chest with a pair of scissors around 8:30 pm.

The attack was reportedly motivated by a previous enmity; Mitul had allegedly slapped someone from the market during a quarrel two days prior.

Police recovered the body and sent it to the Sir Salimullah Medical College Mitford Hospital morgue for an autopsy.

Following the incident, several hundred agitated people, including the victim's relatives, held a procession from Sadarghat to Mitford Hospital.

Mitul was identified as a Jatiotabadi Swechchhasebak Dal activist of Dhaka Metropolitan South’s Ward 37.
